# **1\. Executive Summary**

1.1. Problem Statement

The demand for collaborative computation without mutual disclosure of confidential data (privacy-preserving computation) is growing rapidly, for example distributed PIN verification without leaking credentials. Secure Two-Party Computation (2PC) based on Yao's Garbled Circuits (GC) is a trusted solution, and general-purpose frameworks have made it practical to deploy \[5\]. However, GC evaluation in software places a heavy load on the CPU \[2\]. Conventional hardware architectures are prone to memory explosion because they instantiate the entire logic netlist (combinational netlist) at once, consuming gigabytes of RAM \[3\].

1.2. Proposed Solution

GarbleChip adopts an innovative Sequential Circuit Garbling approach, inspired by the TinyGarble concept \[3\]. Instead of executing a bloated circuit, the algorithm is converted into a compact Finite State Machine with Datapath (FSMD). The FPGA memory only needs to hold the wire labels that are currently active (the cut-width), and registers (D flip-flops) carry wire labels between clock cycles without additional cryptographic operations. Keeping only live wires in an on-chip scratchpad follows the same idea as the sliding wire window used in recent GC accelerators \[1\].

As its main cryptographic engine, GarbleChip uses SHA-256 for Half-Gates evaluation. The 160-bit input, consisting of a 128-bit wire label and a 32-bit Gate ID, fits within a single 512-bit SHA-256 compression block. SHA-256 provides a well-studied and area-efficient option for the hardware implementation \[6\]. As a result :

* One encrypted AND gate is evaluated with a single hash operation (64 clock cycles).  
* XOR gates are computed instantly (0 cycles) thanks to the Free-XOR technique.  
* State/memory stays small (only a few kilobytes of BRAM) using a Sliding Wire Window architecture \[1\].

1.3. Implementation on DE 10-Nano (HPS-FPGA Co-Design)

* ARM Cortex-A9 (HPS) : handles the software-side control and prepares the sequential circuit data, including the garbled tables, before streaming them to the FPGA.  
* FPGA Fabric (Cyclone V) : acts as the hardware acceleration engine for garbled circuit evaluation. Data is transferred from the HPS through the HPS-to-FPGA bridges using Avalon-MM/FIFO interfaces. The bridges support 32/64/128-bit data paths, while the lightweight bridge provides a 32-bit interface for control and status registers \[10\]. Platform Designer is used to connect the HPS and FPGA components through the required AXI-to-Avalon-MM adapters \[9\].

1.4. New Feature & Advantages

| Feature | Advantage |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Hardware-based Evaluator**. Prior FPGA work mainly accelerates the garbler \[2\]. GarbleChip puts the evaluator on the FPGA and the garbler on the ARM HPS. | Offloads the edge-device side of the protocol. |
| **SHA-256 as the garbling hash**. AND-gate tables are decrypted with the competition's SHA-256 core instead of a separate cipher \[6\]. | Reuses a standard, well-studied primitive and keeps the design small. |
| **Free-XOR.** XOR gates need no hash. | Fewer cycles and less area for most of the circuit. |
| **Small on-chip memory.** Only the currently active wire labels are kept (sliding wire window) \[1\]. | A few kilobytes of BRAM instead of storing the whole circuit. |
| **HPS-FPGA co-design.** The ARM garbles and streams, and the FPGA evaluates, over the Avalon bridge \[7\]. | A live two-party demo (Private PIN Authentication) on a single board. |

# **2\. Background and Research Question**

2.1. Background

In national digital identity and security printing infrastructure (the PERURI ecosystem), credential verification at conventional terminals requires absolute trust in the server. With Garbled Circuits, verification becomes Zero-Trust, PIN equality is proven without the server or the terminal exposing each other's secret data. Dedicated hardware for this workload has so far been explored mainly for garbling and general-purpose secure processors \[2\], \[4\].

2.2. Problem Formulation and Design Challenges

* How can 128-bit wire labels be managed to prevent memory explosion while keeping FPGA resource usage below 10% of the DE10-Nano’s ALMs?  
* How can a standard SHA-256 core be adapted as a PRF for efficient Half-Gates evaluation with minimal hardware overhead?  
* How can the HPS-FPGA dataflow be designed to keep the FPGA continuously processing without stalling while waiting for the ARM processor?

# **3\. Proposed Chip Design**

## 3.1. Solution & System Architecture

**Diagram Block System:**  
![][image2]

**RTL Module Details:**

1. **sha256\_core\_iterative.v:** Adapted from the baseline competition (32-bit single-round datapath). Rotates the message schedule in-place without unrolling. Operates in exactly 64 clock cycles per AND gate decryption.  
2. **garble\_gate\_fsm.v:** A sequential controller that manages the bypass for XOR gates (0-cycle), executes PRF/SHA-256 operations for AND gates, and orchestrates the D-Flip-Flop label transfer (state transfer) for the t+1 cycle.  
3. **sliding\_wire\_window\_ram.v:** M10K memory cache that holds active wire labels based on the cut-width range. Ensures memory requirements remain static and isolated from the total circuit depth/length.  
4. **avalon\_stream\_rx.v:** DMA synchronization interface with the HPS clock domain.

**FPGA Resource Utilization Estimate:**

| Resource Component | Estimated Usage | DE10-Nano Capacity |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Logic Elements / LUT | \~2,350 ALM | 110,000 LEs / 41,910 ALMs |
| Registers / Flip-Flops (FF) | \~2,650 FF (\<1%) | 415,000 |
| Block RAM (M10K) | 8 M10K (80 Kbits) (1.4%) | 5,570 Kbits |
| DSP Blocks | 0 DSP (0%) | 112 DSP |

**Software & Design Tools:**  
Intel Quartus Prime (Synthesis & STA), ModelSim / Verilator (RTL Simulation), Platform Designer / Qsys (Avalon Interconnect System), Yosys (EDA Logic Synthesis for *Netlist*), and Python & C (for Golden Model and HPS programming).

## 3.2. Testing Plan

**RTL Simulation:**  
Development of a script-based automated testbench to match the SHA-256 RTL output against the Python Golden Model (bit-exact verification using NIST vectors). The simulation will cover FSMD state transitions from D-Flip-Flop instructions, corner-case scenarios for Half-Gates decryption, and clock synchronization latency evaluation.

**DE10-Nano FPGA Board Hardware Testing:**  
Top-level synthesis process in Quartus and bitstream implementation onto the Cyclone V. On-board testing will validate the DMA (Avalon-MM) streaming pipeline between the C-program in the Linux ARM HPS and the *fabric* accelerator. SignalTap Logic Analyzer will be utilized to detect *pipeline stalls* in real-time.

**Target Success Metrics:**  
100% functional decryption accuracy, purely static BRAM limitation dictated by the circuit's *cut-width*, and a minimum throughput speedup efficiency of 15x compared to pure algorithmic software execution on the ARM Cortex-A9.
